title: introduce-synthetic-batch-primer-and-quant-tier-autoscaler
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a tenant-scoped synthetic batching primer and a quantization-tier autoscaler. Feature gated; safe rollout plan included.
commits: a1b2c3d - add synthetic batch primer core loop and config schema
b2c3d4e - wire primer into request router with opt-in feature flag
c3d4e5f - introduce quant tier autoscaler and tenant policy evaluator
d4e5f6a - add e2e and unit tests; update docs and telemetry
description:
Context and motivation: Production workloads with spiky short sequences often underutilize batching opportunities for a small window after cold starts or during tenant bursts. Existing heuristics rely on observed prior samples which can be brittle for new tenants or highly bursty traffic. This PR introduces a synthetic batch primer: a lightweight poster-child sampler that synthesizes safe, latency-friendly prefill events to increase batching efficiency for the first 5–20 requests without changing user-visible outputs. It also introduces a tenant-scoped quantization-tier autoscaler that recommends/rolls tenant quantization candidates (INT8/FP16/FP32) based on real-time unit-econ signals and simulated downstream quality regressions.

What changed (high level): 1) serving/batcher/synthetic_primer.py: new component that generates ephemeral, internal "primer" tokens for warmup (configurable per-tenant and opt-in by feature flag). Primer runs on a separate lightweight execution path that uses existing KV cache semantics to avoid model-state divergence. 2) serving/quant/autoscaler.py: a controller that consumes token-level cost telemetry and eval-signal feedback (from hedged traffic) and proposes safe quantization tier changes with rollback guards and a canary percentage. 3) console/feature_flags.yaml: new feature flag synthetic_batch_primer (default off) and quant_autoscale_beta flag. 4) telemetry/batch_metrics.proto: taxonomy extension for primer-specific metrics (primer_count, primer_latency_ms, primer_effective_batch_increase). 5) docs/ops/quant-tiers.md and README updates describe operational knobs and the safe rollout plan. 6) tests/e2e/test_synthetic_primer.py: end-to-end smoke tests that assert no user-visible output changes and measure batch delta.

Design notes and safety: The primer sends internal "prefill" tokens that are stripped before model output is materialized. The algorithm ensures determinism: if a request would have used a primer, both primer and non-primer paths produce identical final outputs because primers only prefill KV caches with tokens that match a canonical empty prefix expansion (implementation detail: primer uses a single shared synthetic token id that maps to a stable, no-op embedding). Quant autoscaler decisions are advisory by default — they emit proposed quantization tiers to the console and to a tenant policy engine. When the policy is set to auto-apply for a tenant, the autoscaler performs staged canaries (1%, 10%, 50%) with latent-quality monitors (evals on a small hedged shadow set) before committing. All autoscaler actions are reversible via policy and include rollback triggers based on KL divergence and production derivation tests.

Example primer pseudocode snippet included in the implementation: "for tenant_request in incoming: if feature_flag.enabled(tenant): if primer.should_inject(tenant_request): inject_primer_kv(tenant_request.session_id) router.route(tenant_request)". The actual implementation isolates the primer into a different scheduler queue so primer scheduling doesn't delay user-facing requests.

Telemetry and observability: new metrics and traces are emitted under batch.primer.* and quant.autoscaler.*. CI and staging runs include a synthetic load harness to validate primer impact. In internal benchmarking on c4-gpu-1 instances we observed: median latency increase <1ms for primer path, batching gain of +18% effective tokens/second on cold sequences, and simulated token-level unit-econ improvement of ~12% for typical chat workloads. Quant autoscaler can identify high-confidence INT8 candidates for ~35% of tenants with low quality delta (measured via held-out prompts), and the recommended staged rollout reduced regressive incidents in canaries by 8% compared to manual pilots.

Testing: Unit tests cover primer decision logic, KV isolation, and no-op embedding mapping. E2E tests run against the synthetic load harness and assert output-roundtrip equality. Autoscaler unit tests include simulated tenant telemetry and mock evaluators for KL/divergence triggers. CI pipeline added a specialized job ci/pipeline/batch_autoscale_check.yml that runs the primer e2e in a containerized emulation; CI passed on the final push (flaky test retried once and succeeded).

Files changed summary (small snippets): 1) serving/batcher/synthetic_primer.py - ~230 lines, core algorithm plus config parsing. 2) serving/quant/autoscaler.py - ~180 lines, state machine for proposal -> canary -> commit -> rollback. 3) docs/ops/quant-tiers.md - added operational playbook. 4) telemetry/batch_metrics.proto - added three new gauge/counter entries. 5) tests/e2e/test_synthetic_primer.py - asserts primer injection off produces identical outputs and primer on increases batch size for simulated cold sequences.

Review conversation (high level): - Diego Ramos (reviewer): "Can you confirm the primer won't introduce any cache poisoning vectors? We should validate that synthetic token ids cannot collide with produced embeddings from models." Maya: "We implemented a hard-coded no-op token id and added assertions in KV store to reject collisions. Added unit test to assert mapping is preserved across restarts." - Priya Natarajan: "Autoscaler seems complex; can we make the default mode 'suggest' rather than 'apply' for tenants?" Maya: "Yes — feature flag default is suggest. Auto-apply requires explicit tenant policy. Updated docs to emphasize opt-in for auto-apply." - Noah Fisher: "CI showed a transient e2e flake; can we stabilize with retry/better harness?" Maya: "Added a retry to the harness and increased harness timeout; re-ran CI and green." Review approvals: Diego approved on 2026-02-28, Priya requested a doc tweak which was addressed, Noah approved after CI stabilization.

Risk and rollback: Feature is feature-flag gated. Immediate rollback path: disable synthetic_batch_primer in console and revert autoscaler auto-apply. The PR includes a monitoring playbook: alert on primer_effective_batch_increase < 0 (i.e., primer hurting batching), and on quant.autoscaler.kl_alert > threshold. Owners: @maya (author), @diego (runtime lead). Rollout plan: enable as suggest-only for 10% tenants in staging, run for 48h, then promote to beta for 100 tenants with auto-apply disabled, monitor for 7 days, then consider graduated auto-apply with strict policy rules.

Related work: ENG-4823 tracks the autoscaler productization; PM-129 requested a mechanism for safe tenant quant rollout as part of Q2 roadmap. This PR implements the initial conservative design and documentation for operators.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2026-03-02 after approvals and green CI. Follow-ups: http API to expose proposal history (planned in a follow-up PR), tenant CLI to opt-in/opt-out (follow-up), and extended telemetry retention for canary rollouts (ops ticket created).
